reference.source: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology / WHO Classification of Endocrine Tumours
clinicalPearls: One of the most aggressive human malignancies, typically presenting in elderly patients as a rapidly enlarging, hard, fixed neck mass over weeks
Airway compromise is the dominant early threat, with stridor, dyspnoea, dysphagia, and hoarseness from tracheal and recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
Often arises through dedifferentiation of a pre-existing differentiated thyroid carcinoma or long-standing goitre, frequently accumulating TP53 and TERT promoter mutations
Histology shows undifferentiated spindle, giant, or epithelioid cells with brisk mitoses and necrosis, losing thyroid differentiation markers so it does not concentrate iodine
Because it is not iodine-avid, radioactive iodine is ineffective and management centres on urgent airway assessment, tissue diagnosis, and multimodal therapy
All cases are considered stage IV by convention given the near-universal advanced behaviour at diagnosis
BRAF V600E-mutated tumours may respond to targeted BRAF-directed therapy, so molecular testing should be expedited
reference.pathophysiology: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is an undifferentiated malignancy of follicular-cell origin that has lost the features of differentiated thyroid cancer, including iodine uptake and thyroglobulin production. It commonly evolves from a pre-existing papillary or follicular carcinoma or a long-standing goitre through progressive genetic hits, characteristically TP53 inactivation and TERT promoter mutations superimposed on earlier BRAF or RAS alterations. The result is a highly proliferative, invasive tumour that rapidly infiltrates the trachea, oesophagus, strap muscles, and great vessels of the neck and disseminates widely, so local airway obstruction and distant metastasis appear early.
additionalInvestigations: Urgent airway assessment including flexible laryngoscopy and cross-sectional imaging of the neck and thorax
Core or open biopsy for definitive tissue diagnosis when aspiration is inconclusive
Immunohistochemistry to distinguish it from lymphoma, medullary carcinoma, and metastases
Expedited molecular testing including BRAF V600E to identify targetable disease
Staging cross-sectional or functional imaging to define distant metastasis
Serum calcium and thyroid function as part of baseline assessment
redFlags: Impending airway obstruction with stridor or dyspnoea requiring emergency airway evaluation
Rapidly enlarging fixed neck mass in an elderly patient
New hoarseness or dysphagia indicating invasion of the recurrent laryngeal nerve or oesophagus
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is dismal, with median survival typically only a few months; occasional patients with resectable, intrathyroidal disease or a targetable mutation such as BRAF V600E may survive longer with multimodal treatment.
pitfalls: Delaying airway assessment while awaiting a full diagnostic work-up in a patient with a rapidly growing mass
Mistaking anaplastic carcinoma for lymphoma, which has a very different and far more favourable treatment, without immunohistochemistry
Expecting benefit from radioactive iodine in a tumour that no longer concentrates iodine
Omitting rapid BRAF testing and thereby missing an opportunity for targeted therapy
references: WHO Classification of Endocrine and Neuroendocrine Tumours
